views.name: job_postings_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  c.name AS name,
  c.link AS link,
  c.link_google AS link_google,
  c.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  j.job_title_short AS job_title_short,
  j.job_title AS job_title,
  j.job_location AS job_location,
  j.job_via AS job_via,
  j.job_schedule_type AS job_schedule_type,
  j.job_work_from_home AS job_work_from_home,
  j.search_location AS search_location,
  j.job_posted_date AS job_posted_date,
  -- try to normalize posting date to YYYY-MM-DD when possible; keep original if not parseable
  (CASE
     WHEN length(trim(j.job_posted_date)) >= 10 THEN substr(trim(j.job_posted_date),1,10)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS posted_date_iso,
  j.job_no_degree_mention AS job_no_degree_mention,
  j.job_health_insurance AS job_health_insurance,
  j.job_country AS job_country,
  j.salary_rate AS salary_rate,
  j.salary_year_avg AS salary_year_avg,
  j.salary_hour_avg AS salary_hour_avg
FROM job_postings_fact j
LEFT JOIN job_company c
  ON j.company_id = c.company_id
views.description: Denormalized job postings with company metadata and basic parsed/posting-date fields. Use this when answering questions that need job details together with company attributes and standardized posting date parts. | Use for: Jobs by company and posting date; Salary summaries by company/region; Counts of remote (job_work_from_home) or benefits flags by company; Filtering job postings by parsed posted_date_iso

views.name: job_skills_expanded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  j.job_id,
  j.company_id,
  j.job_title_short AS job_title_short,
  j.job_location AS job_location,
  j.job_country AS job_country,
  s.skill_id AS skill_id,
  sd.skills AS skills,
  sd.type AS type
FROM skills_job_dim s
LEFT JOIN job_postings_fact j
  ON s.job_id = j.job_id
LEFT JOIN skills_dim sd
  ON s.skill_id = sd.skill_id
views.description: Bridge of job postings to skill names. One row per job-skill pair including job company and basic job metadata. Use when analyzing skills demand across jobs or companies. | Use for: Top skills demanded across all job postings; Skill distribution by country or location; Companies hiring for specific skills

views.name: legislators_latest_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus
FROM (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY id_bioguide
      ORDER BY (CASE WHEN length(term_end)>=10 THEN substr(term_end,1,10) ELSE term_end END) DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM legislators_terms
) lt
WHERE lt.rn = 1
views.description: Latest term per legislator (by term_end interpreted as date). Use when you need the most recent term information per legislator for current-state joins or summaries. | Use for: Current party/state/district for each legislator; Joining legislator core attributes to their latest term; Counts of legislators by party using latest term

views.name: legislators_core_with_latest_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.full_name AS full_name,
  l.first_name AS first_name,
  l.last_name AS last_name,
  l.middle_name AS middle_name,
  l.nickname AS nickname,
  l.suffix AS suffix,
  l.other_names_end AS other_names_end,
  l.other_names_middle AS other_names_middle,
  l.other_names_last AS other_names_last,
  l.birthday AS birthday,
  l.gender AS gender,
  l.id_bioguide AS id_bioguide,
  l.id_bioguide_previous_0 AS id_bioguide_previous_0,
  l.id_govtrack AS id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr AS id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia AS id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata AS id_wikidata,
  l.id_google_entity_id AS id_google_entity_id,
  l.id_house_history AS id_house_history,
  l.id_house_history_alternate AS id_house_history_alternate,
  l.id_thomas AS id_thomas,
  l.id_cspan AS id_cspan,
  l.id_votesmart AS id_votesmart,
  l.id_lis AS id_lis,
  l.id_ballotpedia AS id_ballotpedia,
  l.id_opensecrets AS id_opensecrets,
  l.id_fec_0 AS id_fec_0,
  l.id_fec_1 AS id_fec_1,
  l.id_fec_2 AS id_fec_2,
  t.term_id AS term_id,
  t.term_type AS term_type,
  t.term_start AS term_start,
  t.term_end AS term_end,
  t.state AS state,
  t.district AS district,
  t.class AS class,
  t.party AS party,
  t.office AS office
FROM legislators l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT *,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY id_bioguide
        ORDER BY (CASE WHEN length(term_end)>=10 THEN substr(term_end,1,10) ELSE term_end END) DESC
      ) AS rn
    FROM legislators_terms
  ) WHERE rn = 1
) t
  ON l.id_bioguide = t.id_bioguide
views.description: Legislators core attributes joined to their latest term (one row per legislator). Use for person-level profiles including most-recent office details. | Use for: Profiles of current legislators including office and party; Mapping legislator biographic data to their current district/state; Counts or aggregations by party using latest-term join

views.name: cities_countries_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  cc.created_on AS created_on
FROM cities_countries cc
views.description: Countries with core geographic attributes (one row per country_code_2) for joining to city-level data or external location filters. | Use for: Country lookups by code or name; Joining country attributes to cities or currencies; Counts of countries by region/sub_region

views.name: cities_with_country
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ci.city_id AS city_id,
  ci.city_name AS city_name,
  ci.latitude AS latitude,
  ci.longitude AS longitude,
  ci.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  ci.capital AS capital,
  ci.population AS population,
  ci.insert_date AS insert_date,
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region
FROM cities ci
LEFT JOIN cities_countries cc
  ON ci.country_code_2 = cc.country_code_2
views.description: City rows augmented with country attributes by country_code_2. Use for city-level analyses needing country/regional context. | Use for: City populations by country or region; Maps or geospatial joins using city lat/long with country context; Filtering capitals vs non-capitals per country

views.name: aliens_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  TRIM(first_name) AS first_name,
  TRIM(last_name) AS last_name,
  TRIM(email) AS email,
  TRIM(gender) AS gender,
  TRIM(type) AS type,
  birth_year AS birth_year
FROM aliens
views.description: Canonicalized core alien entity table: trims text fields and preserves key identifiers. Use when analyzing alien population or joining to other alien-related tables. | Use for: Counts of aliens by type or gender; Joining alien core to details/location tables; Age or birth-year distributions (requires birth_year)

views.name: job_postings_country_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  job_country AS job_country,
  COUNT(job_id) AS job_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_work_from_home = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS remote_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_no_degree_mention = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_degree_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_health_insurance = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS health_insurance_count
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY job_country
views.description: Aggregated job-level measures by job_country (counts and average salaries). Use for country-level job supply and salary summaries. | Use for: Job counts and average salaries by country; Proportion of remote jobs by country; Country-level benefits or degree-mention prevalence
